run.question: 配置的业务数据库里有哪些表？orders 表里每种 status 的订单各有多少条、failed 占比多少？请用数据库只读查询工具核实后回答。

report.summary: The configured PostgreSQL database exposes exactly one table in the read-only listing: public.orders (columns id, customer, status, amount). Grouping orders by status at query time gives paid 144, failed 72, refunded 24; a separate aggregate confirms 240 total rows, 72 failed and 0 rows with a NULL status, so failed accounts for 30.00% of all orders. These figures describe the database as it is at query time (observed 2026-11-20T21:21:26–28Z), not its contents during the authorized incident window, and they are inventory counts, not a health or error-rate assessment of any service.

claims.text: The read-only table listing of the configured PostgreSQL database returned one user table: public.orders (type table). No other table or view was returned in that listing.

public.orders has 4 columns: id integer NOT NULL, customer character varying(40) nullable, status character varying(16) nullable, amount numeric(10,2) nullable; its only index is the primary-key unique index orders_pkey on id, and it has no foreign keys.

Grouping public.orders by status returned exactly three status values with these row counts: paid 144, failed 72, refunded 24 (query SELECT status, count(*) ... GROUP BY status, 3 rows returned, result not truncated).
An aggregate over public.orders returned total 240, failed 72, failed_pct 30.00 and null_status 0, so the failed share of orders is 30.00% and no order row has a NULL status.

All three database views record their read at query time (observed 2026-11-20T21:21:25Z to 2026-11-20T21:21:28Z) and state that they show the database as it is now, not as it was during the authorized window ending 2026-11-20T21:21:22Z.

gaps: The orders counts are point-in-time snapshots taken at approximately 2026-11-20T21:21:26–28Z, after the authorized window ended (2026-11-20T21:21:22Z); the same counts during the incident window are unknown, and I did not query historical order data.
The table listing returned only one user table at query time and was not truncated, but tables invisible to the read-only account, or other schemas not surfaced, are unknown.
Whether a 30% failed-order share is abnormal for this database has no baseline here: no prior-period order counts or application order metrics were queried in this Run.
next_steps: If the failed-order proportion matters for an incident, compare it against a baseline (earlier order counts or the application's order/transaction metrics) rather than treating the current snapshot as a trend.

query.sql: SELECT status, count(*) AS n FROM orders GROUP BY status ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 100

SELECT count(*) AS total, count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'failed') AS failed, round(100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE status = 'failed') / count(*), 2) AS failed_pct, count(*) FILTER (WHERE status IS NULL) AS null_status FROM orders
